message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** for launching a Google Cloud Compute Engine VM that is as close as possible to an “RTX A6000 + Ubuntu 20.04 LTS” machine.  
(At the time of writing Google Cloud does **not** offer an RTX A6000 GPU – the closest available GPUs are the **NVIDIA Tesla A100** or **A30**.  The example uses the A100, but you can swap it for the A30 if you prefer.)

---

## 1.  Prerequisites

| Item | What to do |
|------|------------|
| **Project** | Create a GCP project (or use an existing one). |
| **Billing** | Enable billing for the project. |
| **Compute Engine API** | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` |
| **GPU quota** | Request a GPU quota increase for the region you plan to use (e.g. `us-central1`). |
| **OAuth 2.0 token** | If you’re calling the REST API directly, obtain an access token (`gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`). |

---

## 2.  gcloud CLI command

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu20"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
  --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata="enable-oslogin=TRUE" \
  --tags="http-server,https-server" \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
```

> **Why these flags?**  
> * `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs / 30 GB RAM – plenty for most workloads.  
> * `nvidia-tesla-a100` is the GPU type.  
> * `ubuntu-2004-lts` pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image.  
> * `pd-ssd` gives fast persistent storage.  
> * `maintenance-policy=TERMINATE` ensures the VM is stopped (not pre‑empted) if the host is reclaimed.  

---

## 3.  REST API (curl) example

If you prefer to use the raw Compute Engine REST API, here’s a minimal JSON payload and a `curl` command that will create the same instance.

### 3.1  JSON payload (`instance.json`)

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu20",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/ubuntu-2004-focal-v20230901"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "enable-oslogin",
        "value": "TRUE"
      }
    ]
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE"
  }
}
```

> **Tip:** Replace `my-gcp-project` with your actual project ID.  
> The `acceleratorType` URL is constructed as `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/{type}`.

### 3.2  curl command

```bash
# Get an access token (once per session)
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# POST the instance
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> **What happens?**  
> The API will return a `operation` resource.  Poll it until `status == DONE` to confirm the instance is ready.

---

## 4.  Quick sanity check

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
# SSH
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu20 --zone us-central1-a

# Inside the VM
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the NVIDIA A100 GPU listed (or the A30 if you swapped the type).

---

## 5.  Notes & Gotchas

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **“GPU type not found”** | Double‑check the accelerator type string.  Use `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone us-central1-a` to see available GPUs. |
| **Quota exceeded** | Request a GPU quota increase for the chosen region. |
| **Billing error** | Ensure the project has an active billing account. |
| **Image not found** | Use the latest image family: `ubuntu-2004-lts`. |
| **Network firewall** | If you need HTTP/HTTPS access, add the `http-server` and `https-server` tags (or open ports manually). |

---

## 6.  Summary

* **gcloud CLI**: quickest, handles auth automatically.  
* **REST API**: gives you full control and is useful for automation scripts.  
* **GPU type**: use `nvidia-tesla-a100` (or `nvidia-tesla-a30`) – RTX A6000 is not currently offered by GCP.  

Happy GPU‑computing! 🚀
